summary: Build IIoT, OEE, and predictive maintenance skills in 5 days. Learn to design smarter plants and improve decision-making.
lede: Smart manufacturing connects sensors, control systems and production data to improve visibility into plant operations. For manufacturing, automation and reliability professionals, this training supports planning connected operations and turning production data into practical decisions. Learners map IIoT data flows, analyze OEE and downtime, and design condition-monitoring or predictive-maintenance workflows using systems such as SCADA, MES and historians.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with plant data, automation systems, or manufacturing performance improvement and need a smarter way to connect them. Manufacturing Engineers who need to connect IIoT data to line performance decisions. Industrial Automation Engineers who manage PLC, SCADA, and edge connectivity layers. Reliability Engineers who track equipment health and predict failure patterns. Plant Managers who need better visibility into throughput, downtime, and OEE. Operations Excellence Managers who coordinate smart factory improvement initiatives. Maintenance Supervisors who translate sensor alerts into work order priorities. Production Supervisors who monitor line disruptions and recurring quality losses. Industrial Data Analysts who build dashboards from machine and historian data. Digital Transformation Managers who scope Industry 4.0 use cases across plants. OT Cybersecurity Specialists who protect connected assets and sensor networks.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of manufacturing operations, automation environments, or maintenance workflows, plus familiarity with production data such as downtime, throughput, scrap, or energy use. Prior exposure to SCADA, PLC concepts, MES, or reliability engineering is helpful. No programming is required to complete the course, although familiarity with dashboards, spreadsheets, or industrial data reports will help you move faster. Advanced topics such as digital twins and AI-assisted condition monitoring are taught at the operational application level, not as engineering-deployment training.
